doc.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: The challenge of Oscar Peterson's trio arrangements
summary: Six almost seven years with Peterson; complicated memorized arrangements pushed Ellis and Ray Brown to the limit.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: That’s great. When you got the chance to play with Oscar Peterson, that was what a five year stretch?
What kind of challenge was that musically in that group?

Oh my gosh it’s hard to describe. We had a lot of arrangements and they weren’t just charts that you’ve got a head, they were really complicated. And you had to remember them all, because we didn’t write it down. And Oscar made, he didn’t purposely make it — but he used to know about how much Ray and I could play, and he’d give us right up to the hilt.
So there was a lot of like not written out, but ensemble things, in addition to the melodies you had to remember.
